1	//! # xerj-wasm
2	//!
3	//! Pluggable transform pipeline for xerj.
4	//!
5	//! Provides a trait-based plugin system for document transformation at ingest
6	//! time.  Built-in plugins (field rename, drop, add, JSON parse, timestamp
7	//! parse, PII redaction, grok, route) are always available as native Rust
8	//! code.
9	//!
10	//! A real WASM backend (via `wasmtime`) can be wired in later behind the
11	//! `wasm` feature flag without changing any public API.
12	
13	pub mod builtins;
14	pub mod pipeline;
15	
16	// ── Re-exports ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
17	
18	pub use pipeline::{ErrorPolicy, Pipeline, PipelineConfig, PipelineStageConfig, ProcessAction};
19	
20	// ── Core trait ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
21	
22	/// A transform plugin — implemented by built-in Rust transforms (and, in the
23	/// future, WASM modules).
24	///
25	/// Plugins are `Send + Sync` so they can be shared across async tasks and
26	/// stored in `Arc<dyn TransformPlugin>`.
27	pub trait TransformPlugin: Send + Sync {
28	    /// Unique name used to reference this plugin in pipeline configs.
29	    fn name(&self) -> &str;
30	
31	    /// Transform `doc` in-place and return the action to take.
32	    ///
33	    /// - [`ProcessAction::Pass`]  — continue to the next stage.
34	    /// - [`ProcessAction::Drop`]  — discard this document entirely.
35	    /// - [`ProcessAction::Route`] — send the document to a different target
36	    ///   index.
37	    fn process(&self, doc: &mut serde_json::Value) -> ProcessAction;
38	}
39	
40	// ── Error type ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
41	
42	use thiserror::Error;
43	
44	#[derive(Debug, Error)]
45	pub enum WasmError {
46	    #[error("pipeline '{0}' not found")]
47	    PipelineNotFound(String),
48	
49	    #[error("plugin '{0}' not found")]
50	    PluginNotFound(String),
51	
52	    #[error("invalid plugin config for '{plugin}': {reason}")]
53	    InvalidConfig { plugin: String, reason: String },
54	
55	    /// The stage type is legitimate but this build does not implement it.
56	    ///
57	    /// Issue #204 keeps this separate from [`WasmError::InvalidConfig`]: a
58	    /// caller who wrote a valid Elasticsearch processor xerj has not
59	    /// implemented has not made a mistake, and must not be told they have.
60	    /// What must never happen is the third option the code used to take —
61	    /// accepting it and quietly running a shorter pipeline.
62	    #[error("unsupported stage type '{stage}'")]
63	    UnsupportedStage { stage: String },
64	
65	    /// The stage type IS implemented, but the caller set an option this build
66	    /// cannot honour — an Elasticsearch processor-level `if` guard, an
67	    /// `on_failure` recovery chain, a `grok` `patterns` array.
68	    ///
69	    /// Issue #204 again, one level down. Reporting these as `InvalidConfig`
70	    /// would tell a caller their valid ES processor is malformed; ignoring them
71	    /// is what the sweep exists to kill — a `set` that runs on documents its
72	    /// `if` excludes is a silently wrong document, not a cosmetic gap. Handled
73	    /// exactly like [`WasmError::UnsupportedStage`] at the API boundary: the
74	    /// definition is accepted (ES accepts it) and recorded as unrunnable, so
75	    /// every ingest through it refuses loudly.
76	    #[error("stage '{stage}': option '{option}' is not supported by this build ({reason})")]
77	    UnsupportedOption {
78	        stage: String,
79	        option: String,
80	        reason: String,
81	    },
82	
83	    /// The pipeline is registered but carries a stage this build cannot run,
84	    /// so no document may pass through it.
85	    #[error("pipeline '{pipeline}' is registered but cannot run: {reason}")]
86	    PipelineNotRunnable { pipeline: String, reason: String },
87	
88	    #[error("plugin error in '{plugin}': {reason}")]
89	    PluginError { plugin: String, reason: String },
90	
91	    #[error(transparent)]
92	    Json(#[from] serde_json::Error),
93	
94	    #[error(transparent)]
95	    Other(#[from] anyhow::Error),
96	}

107	/// How strictly [`Pipeline::from_config`] enforces the issue-#204 contract.
108	///
109	/// The two call sites are not the same situation and must not get the same
110	/// answer:
111	///
112	/// * `Strict` — a caller is on the other end of a `PUT /_ingest/pipeline` and
113	///   can still act on a 400. Anything this build cannot honour is refused.
114	/// * `ReplayPersisted` — boot replay of a definition that is *already* in
115	///   `cluster_state.json`, accepted by whichever build wrote it. There is no
116	///   caller to fail: refusing it turns a working cluster's writes from `201`
117	///   into `400` on a binary upgrade alone, with no `PUT` and no operator
118	///   action. Lucene keys back-compat off the version an index was *created*
119	///   with rather than the running one for exactly this reason
120	///   (`LiveIndexWriterConfig.getIndexCreatedVersionMajor`,
121	///   lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/index/LiveIndexWriterConfig.java:290-298;
122	///   set by `IndexWriterConfig.setIndexCreatedVersionMajor`,
123	///   .../IndexWriterConfig.java:188-220). So replay reproduces the
124	///   *previously shipped* behaviour for the checks this sweep newly added, and
125	///   records every one of them in [`Pipeline::degradations`] so it is loud
126	///   rather than silent.
127	///
128	/// Checks that predate the sweep (a missing required field, an unknown stage
129	/// type) fail in BOTH modes: those definitions did not work before the upgrade
130	/// either.
131	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
132	pub enum CompileMode {
133	    /// Definition time. Refuse anything this build cannot honour.
134	    Strict,
135	    /// Boot replay of an already-persisted definition. Reproduce the
136	    /// pre-sweep behaviour for newly-added checks, and report it.
137	    ReplayPersisted,
138	}

140	impl CompileMode {
141	    fn is_replay(self) -> bool {
142	        matches!(self, Self::ReplayPersisted)
143	    }
144	}

146	impl Pipeline {
147	    /// Build a [`Pipeline`] from a [`PipelineConfig`] at **definition time**.
148	    ///
149	    /// Three outcomes, deliberately distinct (issue #204):
150	    ///
151	    /// - [`WasmError::InvalidConfig`] — the caller's mistake. The definition
152	    ///   must be refused.
153	    /// - [`WasmError::UnsupportedStage`] — a *xerj capability gap*: the caller
154	    ///   wrote something legitimate that we cannot run. The honest answer is to
155	    ///   say so at the point of use rather than pretend either way.
156	    /// - [`WasmError::UnsupportedOption`] — the same gap one level down: the
157	    ///   stage exists, an option on it does not (a processor-level `if` guard,
158	    ///   a `grok` `patterns` array). Silently dropping these is what makes a
159	    ///   compiled pipeline write the wrong document under a `201`.
160	    pub fn from_config(name: impl Into<String>, config: &PipelineConfig) -> Result<Self> {
161	        Self::compile(name, config, CompileMode::Strict)
162	    }
163	
164	    /// Build a [`Pipeline`] from a definition that is **already on disk**.
165	    ///
166	    /// See [`CompileMode::ReplayPersisted`]. Callers MUST surface
167	    /// [`Pipeline::degradations`]; a silent success here would be the same
168	    /// defect this sweep exists to remove, only at boot instead of at `PUT`.
169	    pub fn from_config_replaying_persisted(
170	        name: impl Into<String>,
171	        config: &PipelineConfig,
172	    ) -> Result<Self> {
173	        Self::compile(name, config, CompileMode::ReplayPersisted)
174	    }
175	
176	    fn compile(
177	        name: impl Into<String>,
178	        config: &PipelineConfig,
179	        mode: CompileMode,
180	    ) -> Result<Self> {
181	        let name = name.into();
182	        let mut stages: Vec<Arc<dyn TransformPlugin>> = Vec::new();
183	        let mut degradations: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
184	
185	        for stage_cfg in &config.stages {
186	            let mut stage_degradations: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
187	            let plugin = build_plugin(
188	                &stage_cfg.stage_type,
189	                &stage_cfg.config,
190	                mode,
191	                &mut stage_degradations,
192	            )
193	            .map_err(|e| match e {
194	                StageBuildError::Unsupported(stage) => WasmError::UnsupportedStage { stage },
195	                StageBuildError::UnsupportedOption { option, reason } => {
196	                    WasmError::UnsupportedOption {
197	                        stage: stage_cfg.stage_type.clone(),
198	                        option,
199	                        reason,
200	                    }
201	                }
202	                StageBuildError::Config(reason) => WasmError::InvalidConfig {
203	                    plugin: stage_cfg.stage_type.clone(),
204	                    reason,
205	                },
206	            })?;
207	            degradations.extend(
208	                stage_degradations
209	                    .into_iter()
210	                    .map(|d| format!("stage [{}]: {d}", stage_cfg.stage_type)),
211	            );
212	            stages.push(plugin);
213	        }
214	
215	        Ok(Self {
216	            name,
217	            stages,
218	            degradations,
219	            on_error: config.on_error.clone(),
220	            timeout: if config.timeout_ms == 0 {
221	                Duration::from_secs(30)
222	            } else {
223	                Duration::from_millis(config.timeout_ms)
224	            },
225	        })
226	    }

228	    /// Run `doc` through every stage in order.
229	    ///
230	    /// Returns the first non-[`ProcessAction::Pass`] action, or
231	    /// [`ProcessAction::Pass`] if all stages pass.
232	    pub fn process(&self, doc: &mut Value) -> ProcessAction {
233	        for stage in &self.stages {
234	            debug!(
235	                pipeline = self.name.as_str(),
236	                stage = stage.name(),
237	                "running stage"
238	            );
239	            match stage.process(doc) {
240	                ProcessAction::Pass => continue,
241	                action => {
242	                    debug!(
243	                        pipeline = self.name.as_str(),
244	                        stage = stage.name(),
245	                        action = ?action,
246	                        "stage short-circuits pipeline"
247	                    );
248	                    return action;
249	                }
250	            }
251	        }
252	        ProcessAction::Pass
253	    }

258	    /// affect subsequent documents.

260	        docs.iter_mut().map(|doc| self.process(doc)).collect()

308	            Self::Unsupported(stage) => format!("stage type [{stage}] is not implemented"),

315	/// Read a processor-level boolean whose *written* value decides whether this
316	/// build can honour the processor.
317	///
318	/// `honoured` is the one value this build actually implements. Absence returns
319	/// `Ok(())` — an omitted key is not configuration, and it is what every
320	/// pre-existing definition looks like. A written value that equals `honoured`
321	/// also returns `Ok(())`: **spelling the honoured value out is exactly
322	/// equivalent to omitting it**, and refusing it is what made
323	/// `{"set": {…, "ignore_failure": false}}` — Elasticsearch's own default,
324	/// which ES clients emit verbatim — register a pipeline that 400s every write
325	/// through it. Anything else is a request this build cannot serve.
326	///
327	/// This is Lucene's consume-then-complain shape rather than a presence check:
328	/// `AbstractAnalysisFactory.getBoolean(args, name, defaultVal)`
329	/// (lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/analysis/AbstractAnalysisFactory.java:213-217)
330	/// does `args.remove(name)` and falls back to the default only when the key was
331	/// ABSENT; `ArabicStemFilterFactory`
332	/// (lucene/analysis/common/src/java/org/apache/lucene/analysis/ar/ArabicStemFilterFactory.java:44-51)
333	/// then throws `Unknown parameters` on whatever is LEFT. Presence alone never
334	/// decides anything.
335	fn honoured_bool(
336	    config: &Value,
337	    key: &'static str,
338	    honoured: bool,
339	    reason: &str,
340	) -> std::result::Result<(), StageBuildError> {
341	    match config.get(key) {
342	        None => Ok(()),
343	        Some(Value::Bool(b)) if *b == honoured => Ok(()),
344	        Some(Value::Bool(_)) => Err(StageBuildError::UnsupportedOption {
345	            option: key.to_string(),
346	            reason: reason.to_string(),
347	        }),
348	        Some(other) => Err(StageBuildError::Config(format!(
349	            "'{key}' must be a boolean, got {other}"
350	        ))),
351	    }
352	}

354	/// Processor-level keys that decide **whether** a processor runs or **what
355	/// happens when it fails**, none of which the compiled pipeline can act on.
356	///
357	/// Issue #204, applied to this sweep's own new surface. `PUT /_ingest/pipeline`
358	/// now means "compiled ⇒ xerj honours this"; a `{"set": {…, "if": "ctx.foo ==
359	/// 'never'"}}` that compiles and then sets the field on every document makes
360	/// that promise false, and writes the wrong document under a `201`. The
361	/// pipeline is accepted (ES accepts it) and recorded as unrunnable, so the gap
362	/// surfaces at ingest instead of being silently resolved in the caller's face.
363	///
364	/// `tag` and `description` are deliberately NOT here: they are identification
365	/// metadata that changes no document and no decision on this path.
366	///
367	/// The rule this applies, uniformly: **accept the value this build actually
368	/// implements (and absence, which is not configuration); refuse any other
369	/// written value.** It is the same rule `append`'s `allow_duplicates` already
370	/// used — ES's default there is `true`, which is what `AppendPlugin` does, so
371	/// `true`/absent are accepted and `false` is refused.
372	fn check_unhonourable_processor_keys(config: &Value) -> std::result::Result<(), StageBuildError> {
373	    // `if`: EVERY value changes which documents the processor runs on, and
374	    // none of them is evaluated here. Unlike the booleans below there is no
375	    // spelling of `if` that means "no guard" — that spelling is omitting it.
376	    if config.get("if").is_some() {
377	        return Err(StageBuildError::UnsupportedOption {
378	            option: "if".to_string(),
379	            reason: "the guard is not evaluated, so the processor would run on documents \
380	                     it excludes"
381	                .to_string(),
382	        });
383	    }
384	    // `on_failure`: an EMPTY recovery chain asks for nothing, which is what
385	    // happens. A non-empty one is a chain that would not run.
386	    match config.get("on_failure") {
387	        None => {}
388	        Some(Value::Array(a)) if a.is_empty() => {}
389	        Some(_) => {
390	            return Err(StageBuildError::UnsupportedOption {
391	                option: "on_failure".to_string(),
392	                reason: "the recovery processors are not run; the pipeline's `on_error` \
393	                         policy applies instead"
394	                    .to_string(),
395	            })
396	        }
397	    }
398	    // `ignore_failure`: ES's default is `false` and `false` is what this build
399	    // does — `ProcessAction` has no error variant, so a stage cannot report a
400	    // runtime failure for anything to ignore in the first place. `true` asks
401	    // for a decision this build cannot make.
402	    honoured_bool(
403	        config,
404	        "ignore_failure",
405	        false,
406	        "a failing processor is not ignored; the pipeline's `on_error` policy applies instead",
407	    )
408	}

410	/// `ignore_missing`, for the four stages that read one named field
411	/// (`drop_field`, `field_rename`, `convert`, `timestamp_parse`).
412	///
413	/// Every one of those plugins returns `ProcessAction::Pass` when the field is
414	/// absent — `DropFieldPlugin::process` (`builtins.rs`) calls `obj.remove` and
415	/// moves on; `ConvertTypePlugin::process` returns early on `None`. That is
416	/// exactly `ignore_missing: true`, so `true` is honoured to the letter.
417	/// `false` asks for the document to be FAILED when the field is absent, and
418	/// this build cannot fail a document from inside a stage at all:
419	/// [`ProcessAction`] has no error variant.
420	///
421	/// **Known, documented divergence** (`CHANGELOG.md`, "Known gaps"): when
422	/// `ignore_missing` is OMITTED, ES's default is `false` and xerj still does
423	/// not fail the document. Absence is not configuration — nothing was written
424	/// for this build to break its word on — and refusing it would 400 every ES
425	/// `remove`/`rename`/`convert`/`date` processor ever written. Writing `false`
426	/// explicitly IS configuration, and is refused.
427	fn check_ignore_missing(config: &Value, stage: &str) -> std::result::Result<(), StageBuildError> {
428	    honoured_bool(
429	        config,
430	        "ignore_missing",
431	        true,
432	        &format!(
433	            "xerj's `{stage}` stage passes the document through unchanged when the field is \
434	             absent; failing the document on a missing field is not implemented"
435	        ),
436	    )
437	}

439	/// Instantiate a built-in plugin by name.
440	///
441	/// `mode` decides what happens to config this build cannot honour; see
442	/// [`CompileMode`]. Every check that `ReplayPersisted` waves through pushes one
443	/// line onto `degradations` — the pipeline runs exactly as the previous build
444	/// ran it, and the caller reports that it is doing so.
445	fn build_plugin(
446	    stage_type: &str,
447	    config: &Value,
448	    mode: CompileMode,
449	    degradations: &mut Vec<String>,
450	) -> std::result::Result<Arc<dyn TransformPlugin>, StageBuildError> {
451	    // `soften` turns a refusal into a recorded degradation under
452	    // `ReplayPersisted`, and leaves it a refusal under `Strict`.
453	    macro_rules! soften {
454	        ($err:expr, $legacy:expr) => {{
455	            let e: StageBuildError = $err;
456	            if mode.is_replay() {
457	                degradations.push(e.to_reason());
458	                $legacy
459	            } else {
460	                return Err(e);
461	            }
462	        }};
463	    }
464	    if let Err(e) = check_unhonourable_processor_keys(config) {
465	        soften!(e, ());
466	    }
467	    match stage_type {
468	        "json_parse" => {
469	            let field = str_field(config, "field")?;
470	            let target = config
471	                .get("target")
472	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
473	                .unwrap_or("")
474	                .to_string();
475	            Ok(Arc::new(JsonParsePlugin::new(field, target)))
476	        }
477	
478	        "timestamp_parse" => {
479	            let field = str_field(config, "field")?;
480	            if let Err(e) = check_ignore_missing(config, "timestamp_parse") {
481	                soften!(e, ());
482	            }
483	            let formats = match optional_string_array(config, "formats") {
484	                Ok(v) => v,
485	                Err(e) => soften!(e.into(), None),
486	            }
487	            .unwrap_or_default();
488	            let target = config
489	                .get("target")
490	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
491	                .map(str::to_string);
492	            Ok(Arc::new(TimestampParsePlugin::new(field, formats, target)))
493	        }
494	
495	        "field_rename" => {
496	            if let Err(e) = check_ignore_missing(config, "field_rename") {
497	                soften!(e, ());
498	            }
499	            let mappings = config
500	                .get("mappings")
501	                .and_then(Value::as_object)
502	                .ok_or_else(|| "missing 'mappings' object".to_string())?;
503	            let map: HashMap<String, String> = mappings
504	                .iter()
505	                .filter_map(|(k, v)| v.as_str().map(|s| (k.clone(), s.to_string())))
506	                .collect();
507	            Ok(Arc::new(FieldRenamePlugin::new(map)))
508	        }
509	
510	        "drop_field" => {
511	            if let Err(e) = check_ignore_missing(config, "drop_field") {
512	                soften!(e, ());
513	            }
514	            let fields = string_array(config, "fields")?;
515	            Ok(Arc::new(DropFieldPlugin::new(fields)))
516	        }
517	
518	        "add_field" => {
519	            let field = str_field(config, "field")?;
520	            let value = config
521	                .get("value")
522	                .cloned()
523	                .ok_or_else(|| "missing 'value'".to_string())?;
524	            Ok(Arc::new(AddFieldPlugin::new(field, value)))
525	        }
526	
527	        "route" => {
528	            let field = str_field(config, "field")?;
529	            let routes = config
530	                .get("routes")
531	                .and_then(Value::as_object)
532	                .ok_or_else(|| "missing 'routes' object".to_string())?;
533	            let map: HashMap<String, String> = routes
534	                .iter()
535	                .filter_map(|(k, v)| v.as_str().map(|s| (k.clone(), s.to_string())))
536	                .collect();
537	            let default = config
538	                .get("default")
539	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
540	                .map(str::to_string);
541	            Ok(Arc::new(RoutePlugin::new(field, map, default)))
542	        }
543	
544	        "grok" => {
545	            let field = str_field(config, "field")?;
546	            // Elasticsearch's `grok` processor is driven by `patterns` — an
547	            // ARRAY of grok expressions (`["%{IP:client} %{WORD:method}"]`),
548	            // optionally with `pattern_definitions`. xerj's `grok` is a
549	            // different, narrower thing: one NAMED pattern out of
550	            // `GROK_PATTERN_NAMES`. Reading `pattern` and defaulting to
551	            // `SYSLOG` meant an ES grok processor compiled clean, answered
552	            // `200 acknowledged` under this PR's "compiled ⇒ honoured"
553	            // contract, and left the document untouched (issue #204 — measured:
554	            // `{"message": "10.0.0.1 GET"}` came back with no `client` field).
555	            for key in ["patterns", "pattern_definitions"] {
556	                if config.get(key).is_some() {
557	                    soften!(
558	                        StageBuildError::UnsupportedOption {
559	                            option: key.to_string(),
560	                            reason: format!(
561	                                "xerj's grok stage takes a named `pattern` from [{}], not \
562	                                 arbitrary grok expressions",
563	                                GROK_PATTERN_NAMES.join(", ")
564	                            ),
565	                        },
566	                        ()
567	                    );
568	                }
569	            }
570	            let pattern_name = match config.get("pattern") {
571	                None => "SYSLOG".to_string(),
572	                Some(Value::String(s)) => {
573	                    // Fail closed: an unrecognised pattern name used to fall
574	                    // through to the generic catch-all, which extracts a
575	                    // single `message` field and nothing else (issue #204).
576	                    if !GROK_PATTERN_NAMES.contains(&s.as_str()) {
577	                        soften!(
578	                            format!(
579	                                "unknown grok pattern '{s}' (known patterns: {})",
580	                                GROK_PATTERN_NAMES.join(", ")
581	                            )
582	                            .into(),
583	                            ()
584	                        );
585	                    }
586	                    s.clone()
587	                }

726	                None => false,

728	                Some(v) => soften!(
729	                    format!("'override' must be a boolean, got {v}").into(),
730	                    false

732	            };

774	    config
775	        .get(key)
776	        .and_then(Value::as_str)

781	/// Read an OPTIONAL array-of-strings config key.
782	///
783	/// `Ok(None)` means the key is absent (the caller applies its documented
784	/// default). A present-but-wrong-shaped value is an error rather than a silent
785	/// fall-through to the default — `"formats": "%Y-%m-%d"` used to be dropped by
786	/// `and_then(Value::as_array)` and the stage then behaved as if no formats had
787	/// been configured at all (issue #204).
788	fn optional_string_array(
789	    config: &Value,
790	    key: &str,
791	) -> std::result::Result<Option<Vec<String>>, String> {
792	    let Some(raw) = config.get(key) else {
793	        return Ok(None);
794	    };
795	    let arr = raw
796	        .as_array()
797	        .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{key}' must be an array of strings"))?;
798	    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
799	    for v in arr {
800	        let s = v
801	            .as_str()
802	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("'{key}' must contain only strings, got {v}"))?;
803	        out.push(s.to_string());
804	    }
805	    Ok(Some(out))
806	}
807	
808	fn string_array(config: &Value, key: &str) -> std::result::Result<Vec<String>, String> {
809	    let arr = config
810	        .get(key)
811	        .and_then(Value::as_array)
812	        .ok_or_else(|| format!("missing required array field '{key}'"))?;
813	    Ok(arr
814	        .iter()
815	        .filter_map(|v| v.as_str().map(str::to_string))
816	        .collect())
817	}

208	            .components()

210	            .any(|c| is_hidden_name(c.as_os_str()))
211	        {
212	            return Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenOutsideRoot);
213	        }
214	        return Err(SymlinkVerdict::OutsideRoot(real));
215	    };
216	    // In-root: judge only the part below the root. A brain over a dot-named
217	    // folder still works — that exemption is the same one the walker gives the
218	    // root itself at depth 0.
219	    if rel.components().any(|c| is_hidden_name(c.as_os_str())) {
220	        return Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenTarget);
221	    }
222	    Ok(Some(real))
223	}

294	/// One traversal, two callers: the file inventory and (`dirs_out`) the watch
295	/// set. With `dirs_out` set, every admitted directory is collected and files are
296	/// not examined at all.
297	fn walk_impl(
298	    root: &Path,
299	    follow_symlinks: bool,
300	    allow_outside_root: bool,
301	    ignore: IgnoreOptions,
302	    mut dirs_out: Option<&mut Vec<PathBuf>>,
303	) -> Result<(Vec<FileEntry>, IgnoreReport)> {
304	    let root_canon = root
305	        .canonicalize()
306	        .with_context(|| format!("resolve root folder {}", root.display()))?;
307	    if !root_canon.is_dir() {
308	        anyhow::bail!("{} is not a directory", root_canon.display());
309	    }
310	    let mut out = Vec::new();
311	    // Shallowest depth from which the walk is inside a symlink; see the guard.
312	    let mut link_depth: Option<usize> = None;
313	    let marker_defaults = ignore.enabled && ignore.defaults;
314	    let mut stack = IgnoreStack::new(&root_canon, ignore);
315	    // Manual iteration rather than `filter_entry`, because the ignore stack has
316	    // to load a directory's ignore files *after* that directory is admitted and
317	    // *before* its children are judged. `skip_current_dir` on a just-yielded
318	    // directory prunes its contents — walkdir's own documented pattern, and the
319	    // same effect `filter_entry` had.
320	    let mut it = walkdir::WalkDir::new(&root_canon)
321	        .follow_links(follow_symlinks)
322	        .into_iter();
323	    while let Some(next) = it.next() {
324	        let entry = match next {
325	            Ok(e) => e,
326	            Err(e) => {
327	                // This message renders the offending PATH, and it goes to the
328	                // same stderr an agent parses for `xerj-progress` /
329	                // `xerj-done` records. An unreadable directory whose name
330	                // carries a newline would otherwise start a line here — the
331	                // #278 forgery, through a surface the progress module does not
332	                // own. Sanitised for the same reason and by the same rule.
333	                //
334	                // Routing this through `Progress` as well (so `--quiet` is
335	                // silent and `--progress json` stays one object per line) needs
336	                // a handle the walker does not have; that is a separate change.
337	                eprintln!(
338	                    "walk: skipping unreadable entry: {}",
339	                    crate::progress::sanitize(&e.to_string(), crate::progress::SAFE_PATH_MAX)
340	                );
341	                continue;
342	            }
343	        };
344	        let is_dir = entry.file_type().is_dir();
345	        // Retire the layers of directories this entry is no longer inside; see
346	        // `IgnoreStack::truncate_to` for why every entry needs it, not just
347	        // directories.
348	        stack.truncate_to(entry.depth());
349	        // SECURITY / hygiene: do not index hidden files or descend into hidden
350	        // directories. Without this the walker happily indexed `.env` (secrets,
351	        // API tokens), `.git`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, and other dotfiles into a
352	        // queryable brain with no per-brain authorization — a real exposure for
353	        // the "point it at my project folder" use case. A hidden directory is
354	        // pruned before descending, so `.git/` is skipped whole. The root
355	        // itself (depth 0) is exempt so a brain over a dot-named folder still
356	        // works. `--no-ignore` does NOT turn this off: it is not one of the
357	        // ignore rules, it is the main reason secrets stay out.
358	        //
359	        // The limit of that claim, stated because the rest of this file used to
360	        // assert it without one: this is a rule about NAMES and, under
361	        // `--follow-symlinks`, about where a link RESOLVES. A hard link has
362	        // neither — it is a second directory entry for the same inode, so
363	        // `ln .secretdir/k.txt notes.txt` reads the secret under a visible name
364	        // and nothing here can tell. Defending that needs `(dev, ino)` of every
365	        // hidden-rule exclusion, which a walk that prunes hidden directories
366	        // without descending does not have. `cp -al`, `rsync --link-dest` and
367	        // hard-linked package stores all produce that shape without an attacker.
368	        if entry.depth() > 0 && is_hidden_name(entry.file_name()) {
369	            stack.record_hidden(is_dir);
370	            if is_dir {
371	                it.skip_current_dir();
372	            }
373	            continue;
374	        }
375	        // The rule above judges the NAME the walk arrived by, which is the
376	        // whole rule when links are not followed. Under `--follow-symlinks` it
377	        // is not: a link is free to be called `notes.txt` and point at
378	        // `.secretdir/k.txt`, and walkdir then yields the target's contents
379	        // under the link's visible name. Both halves of the guarantee above
380	        // fail that way — the secret is indexed, and a link to a directory
381	        // outside the root drags in a tree the operator never pointed at
382	        // (`shared -> /etc` indexes `/etc/shadow` as `shared/shadow`). The
383	        // report made it worse by still saying the hidden directories were
384	        // pruned, which was true of the traversal and false of the outcome.
385	        //
386	        // So under the flag the same two questions are asked of the RESOLVED
387	        // path instead of the name. Loop-safety is walkdir's and unrelated;
388	        // this is the secret rule and the root boundary.
389	        // Resolving is only necessary once the walk has actually gone through a
390	        // link. `canonicalize` is `realpath(3)` and issues one `readlinkat` per
391	        // path component, so doing it for every entry costs 8-14 failing
392	        // syscalls per file on an ordinary tree and made the walk 4.2x slower
393	        // with 7.6x the syscalls — all of it wasted on paths where no link
394	        // exists. `link_depth` is the shallowest depth at or below which some
395	        // ancestor (or the entry itself) is a symlink; below that the walk path
396	        // and the real path cannot differ.
397	        if entry.path_is_symlink() {
398	            link_depth = Some(link_depth.map_or(entry.depth(), |d: usize| d.min(entry.depth())));
399	        } else if is_dir && link_depth.is_some_and(|d| entry.depth() <= d) {
400	            link_depth = None;
401	        }
402	        let through_link = entry.path_is_symlink() || link_depth.is_some_and(|d| entry.depth() > d);
403	        // The path every later stage should open. The guard resolves the entry
404	        // to decide on it; keeping that resolution is what stops the decision
405	        // being made about one file and the bytes being read from another.
406	        // `content.rs` hashes and `lib.rs` extracts from `FileEntry::path`
407	        // minutes after the walk on a large corpus, each a fresh `open()` that
408	        // re-follows the link — so a link re-pointed in between handed the
409	        // refused content straight into a document body. `rel` still comes from
410	        // the walk path: that is the name the operator pointed at and the
411	        // identity the index is keyed on.
412	        let mut resolved: Option<PathBuf> = None;
413	        if follow_symlinks && entry.depth() > 0 && through_link {
414	            match escaped_or_hidden_target(&root_canon, entry.path()) {
415	                Ok(real) => resolved = real,
416	                // Admitted by the waiver — but with the RESOLVED path, so the
417	                // bytes read later are the bytes that were judged. This arm was
418	                // empty, which stored the walk path and re-followed the link at
419	                // read time for everything the flag ingests.
420	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::OutsideRoot(real)) if allow_outside_root => {
421	                    resolved = Some(real);
422	                }
423	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenOutsideRoot) => {
424	                    stack.record_symlink_hidden_escape(is_dir);
425	                    if is_dir {
426	                        it.skip_current_dir();
427	                    }
428	                    continue;
429	                }
430	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::OutsideRoot(_)) => {
431	                    stack.record_symlink_escape(is_dir);
432	                    if is_dir {
433	                        it.skip_current_dir();
434	                    }
435	                    continue;
436	                }
437	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::HiddenTarget) => {
438	                    stack.record_hidden(is_dir);
439	                    if is_dir {
440	                        it.skip_current_dir();
441	                    }
442	                    continue;
443	                }
444	                Err(SymlinkVerdict::Unresolvable) => {
445	                    stack.record_symlink_unresolved(is_dir);
446	                    if is_dir {
447	                        it.skip_current_dir();
448	                    }
449	                    continue;
450	                }
451	            }
452	        }
453	        if is_dir {
454	            // The root is never judged by the rules below it: pointing
455	            // autoindex at a folder is an explicit instruction, and the note
456	            // explaining that it *would* have been ignored is on the report.
457	            if entry.depth() > 0 && stack.skip_dir(entry.path()).is_some() {
458	                it.skip_current_dir();
459	                continue;
460	            }
461	            // Marker-gated generated dirs (part of the built-in defaults, so
462	            // `--no-ignore` / `--no-default-ignores` disable it): names like
463	            // Unity's `Library/` or `Logs/` are too common for the blunt
464	            // DEFAULT_IGNORE_PATTERNS, so they are pruned only when a sibling
465	            // marker file proves the parent is that kind of project.
466	            if entry.depth() > 0 && marker_defaults {
467	                if let Some(label) = marker_generated_dir(entry.path()) {
468	                    stack.record_marker_dir(entry.path(), label);
469	                    it.skip_current_dir();
470	                    continue;
471	                }
472	            }
473	            stack.enter_dir(entry.path(), entry.depth());
474	            if let Some(dirs) = dirs_out.as_mut() {
475	                // The path the watcher must watch is the path the walk arrived
476	                // by — the same one `rel` is derived from — so a followed link
477	                // is watched where the operator pointed, not where it resolves.
478	                dirs.push(entry.path().to_path_buf());
479	            }
480	            continue;
481	        }
482	        // Watch-set mode wants directories only; a file's metadata is a syscall
483	        // per entry that nothing on this route reads.
484	        if dirs_out.is_some() {
485	            continue;
486	        }
487	        if !entry.file_type().is_file() {
488	            continue;
489	        }
490	        if stack.skip_file(entry.path()).is_some() {
491	            continue;
492	        }
493	        // Marker-gated Takeout noise (built-in defaults, so `--no-ignore` /
494	        // `--no-default-ignores` disable it). After the ignore files, and
495	        // yielding to them: a `!archive_browser.html` line in `.xerjignore`
496	        // is an explicit instruction and wins.
497	        if marker_defaults {
498	            if let Some(label) = takeout_noise(entry.path()) {
499	                if !stack.is_reincluded(entry.path(), false) {
500	                    stack.record_marker_file(label);
501	                    continue;
502	                }
503	            }
504	        }
505	        let md = match entry.metadata() {
506	            Ok(m) => m,
507	            Err(_) => continue,
508	        };
509	        let p = entry.path().to_path_buf();
510	        let rel = p
511	            .strip_prefix(&root_canon)
512	            .unwrap_or(&p)
513	            .to_string_lossy()
514	            .replace('\\', "/");
515	        let rel_id = stable_path_id(p.strip_prefix(&root_canon).unwrap_or(&p));
516	        out.push(FileEntry {
517	            path: resolved.unwrap_or(p),
518	            rel,
519	            rel_id,
520	            is_symlink: entry
521	                .path()
522	                .symlink_metadata()
523	                .is_ok_and(|m| m.file_type().is_symlink()),
524	            size: md.len(),
525	        });
526	    }
527	    // Deterministic order for clustering / naming.
528	    out.sort_by(|a, b| a.rel.cmp(&b.rel));
529	    Ok((out, stack.report))
530	}
